items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1957-multiple
items.q: he picked up on me and brought me in his band. He had a band there, and I used to play with him all the time.

ctx.x: Raceland, Louisiana, yeah. And so, a fellow by the name of Paul Rozier, like eight miles from my home, he picked up on me and brought me in his band. He had a band there, and I used to play with him all the time. Another fellow named Mike Taylor, one mile from there. And Nick's a fellow from here. Not from here. He's from Raceland, but he's an older man to me named Bo Bo. Used to be a tuba player way back there with Buddy Bowling. And he picked me up in Brompton, New Orleans, one time. And I come in and played a…
Who else was in the band when you went up? Who else played in that band with you?

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-04-04
items.q: old Paul Rozier from Barley-Zellman, Louisiana, he showed me a whole lot too.

ctx.x: Well when you started off with a teacher did the teacher make you practice much? Well guess how that

happened. I didn't have no teacher. Not at noon. And the element we went rehearsal two hours in the morning and two hours in the evening. Where Chip, like I tell you, Chip used to sit right side me and show me a lot of notes see. I didn't know. I ain't gonna lie. I didn't know. But I would anything he'd tell me I remembered. I don't care how long up until the day I can remember anything he told me. Told me what an eight note was, a quarter note was, and how many notes was in the bar and I remember all that see. I…
Well what are some of the different things that they taught you about tonation and fingering?
